digests.title: AI startup ideas — Weekly, 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-09
digests.overview: The clearest pattern this period is a move from making AI output to proving it is right. Several companies formally verify agent queries or math proofs, or build evals that let agent code ship without human review. A second group builds training grounds that score agents against what actually happened, in software and on real robots. AI is also moving into slow, data-poor physical systems such as the distribution grid, and into money flows: claims review, fraud decisions, item pricing and payments started by agents.

digests.title: AI startup ideas — Weekly, 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-01
digests.overview: In this period, many founders sell the finished work itself, such as legal claims, tax credits and schooling, rather than software for doing it. A second group is betting that the next data advantage comes from the physical world: muscle signals, car repairs and permit archives. The agent infrastructure layer is getting more specific, with separate products for per-agent computers, access across company boundaries, and search without embeddings. AI compute costs are now a market of their own, with startups working on ocean data centers, inference auctions and cards built for AI spend.

digests.title: AI startup ideas — 90-day backfill, 2026-07-19 to 2026-10-17
digests.overview: This period's strongest ideas treat AI agents as a new class of user and actor. Startups are building controls that approve, verify, and insure agent actions, and they are rebuilding software, marketplaces, and operating systems so agents can use them directly. A second group treats compute as a commodity that needs exchanges, insurance, and new hardware substrates. A third group sells the data and simulations that frontier and robotics labs need. Many founders also skip software sales: they buy or start the service business (radiology, law, trucking, real estate) and run it with agents.
